But no slightest sign of them ever met our eyes. If the earth told a true story, then Stapleton never reached that island of refuge towards which he struggled through the fog upon that last night. Somewhere in the heart of the great Grimpen Mire, down in the foul slime of the huge morass which had sucked him in, this cold and cruel-hearted man is forever buried.

段.文: 在那座四面环着沼地的小岛上，也就是他藏匿那个凶猛帮凶的地方，我们找到了他留下的许多痕迹。一个巨大的传动轮和一口填了半截垃圾的竖井，表明这里是一座废弃的矿。旁边是矿工住过的小屋，已经坍塌残破，矿工们无疑是被四周沼泽的恶臭熏走的。其中一间小屋里有一个铁环和一条铁链，还有一堆啃过的骨头，说明那畜生曾经被关在这里。碎石堆里躺着一具骨架，上面还粘着一团纠结的棕毛。
段.en: Many traces we found of him in the bog-girt island where he had hid his savage ally. A huge driving-wheel and a shaft half-filled with rubbish showed the position of an abandoned mine. Beside it were the crumbling remains of the cottages of the miners, driven away no doubt by the foul reek of the surrounding swamp. In one of these a staple and chain with a quantity of gnawed bones showed where the animal had been confined. A skeleton with a tangle of brown hair adhering to it lay among the débris.

段.文: “一条狗！”福尔摩斯说，“天哪，是一条卷毛的长毛垂耳猎犬。可怜的莫蒂默再也见不到他的爱犬了。好了，我想这个地方不会再有什么我们还没弄清的秘密了。他能把猎犬藏起来，却没法让它不叫，所以才有了那些就是在白天听来也叫人不舒服的嚎叫。遇到紧急情况，他可以把猎犬关在梅里皮特宅的外屋里，但那总是有风险的。只有到了决定性的那一天，在他看来是他全部努力见分晓的那一天，他才敢这么做。罐子里的这种膏，无疑就是涂在那畜生身上的发光混合物。这个主意当然是从家族魔犬的传说来的，也是想把老查尔斯爵士活活吓死。难怪那个可怜的逃犯会边跑边叫，就像我们的朋友那样，换了我们自己恐怕也会那样，因为他看见这样一个怪物在漆黑的荒原上蹿跳着追他。这个手段真是狡猾。且不说有机会把受害者逼上死路，哪个乡下人要是在荒原上瞧见了这样一个怪物（很多人确实瞧见过），又有谁敢去仔细追究呢？华生，我在伦敦说过，现在我再说一遍：我们帮着追捕过的人里，还没有一个比躺在那边的这个人更危险的。”他说着，伸出长长的手臂，朝那一大片斑驳的、点缀着绿斑的沼地一挥。沼地一直延伸到远处，与荒原赤褐色的山坡连成一片。
段.en: “A dog!” said Holmes. “By Jove, a curly-haired spaniel. Poor Mortimer will never see his pet again. Well, I do not know that this place contains any secret which we have not already fathomed. He could hide his hound, but he could not hush its voice, and hence came those cries which even in daylight were not pleasant to hear. On an emergency he could keep the hound in the out-house at Merripit, but it was always a risk, and it was only on the supreme day, which he regarded as the end of all his efforts, that he dared do it. This paste in the tin is no doubt the luminous mixture with which the creature was daubed. It was suggested, of course, by the story of the family hell-hound, and by the desire to frighten old Sir Charles to death. No wonder the poor devil of a convict ran and screamed, even as our friend did, and as we ourselves might have done, when he saw such a creature bounding through the darkness of the moor upon his track. It was a cunning device, for, apart from the chance of driving your victim to his death, what peasant would venture to inquire too closely into such a creature should he get sight of it, as many have done, upon the moor? I said it in London, Watson, and I say it again now, that never yet have we helped to hunt down a more dangerous man than he who is lying yonder”—he swept his long arm towards the huge mottled expanse of green-splotched bog which stretched away until it merged into the russet slopes of the moor.

段.文: 那是十一月底的一个夜晚，又冷又湿，雾气沉沉。福尔摩斯和我坐在贝克街寓所的起居室里，一边一个，守着熊熊的炉火。德文郡之行以悲剧收场之后，他接手了两件极其重要的案子。头一件，他揭穿了厄普伍德上校在无双俱乐部那桩有名的纸牌丑闻里的卑劣行径；第二件，他为不幸的蒙庞西埃夫人洗清了谋杀罪名。当时她被指控害死了继女卡雷尔小姐，大家也许还记得，这位年轻小姐半年后被人发现活得好好的，已经在纽约结了婚。一连几件又难又重要的案子都办得很成功，我的朋友心情极好，所以我才能劝他谈谈巴斯克维尔疑案的细节。我一直耐心地等着这个机会，因为我知道，他从不让案子互相交叠；他那清晰而讲求逻辑的头脑，也不会从手头的工作中分出心来，去回想过去的事。不过，亨利爵士和莫蒂默医生这时正在伦敦，准备动身作那次长途旅行，那是医生建议他用来恢复受损的神经的。那天下午他们刚来看过我们，所以很自然地，就谈起了这个话题。
段.en: It was the end of November, and Holmes and I sat, upon a raw and foggy night, on either side of a blazing fire in our sitting-room in Baker Street. Since the tragic upshot of our visit to Devonshire he had been engaged in two affairs of the utmost importance, in the first of which he had exposed the atrocious conduct of Colonel Upwood in connection with the famous card scandal of the Nonpareil Club, while in the second he had defended the unfortunate Mme. Montpensier from the charge of murder which hung over her in connection with the death of her step-daughter, Mlle. Carére, the young lady who, as it will be remembered, was found six months later alive and married in New York. My friend was in excellent spirits over the success which had attended a succession of difficult and important cases, so that I was able to induce him to discuss the details of the Baskerville mystery. I had waited patiently for the opportunity for I was aware that he would never permit cases to overlap, and that his clear and logical mind would not be drawn from its present work to dwell upon memories of the past. Sir Henry and Dr. Mortimer were, however, in London, on their way to that long voyage which had been recommended for the restoration of his shattered nerves. They had called upon us that very afternoon, so that it was natural that the subject should come up for discussion.

段.文: “从那个自称斯台普顿的人的角度看，”福尔摩斯说，“整个事情的经过既简单又直接。可是对我们来说，起初根本无从知道他行动的动机，又只能了解到一部分事实，所以一切都显得极其复杂。我有幸跟斯台普顿太太谈过两次，现在案子已经完全水落石出，据我所知，没有什么还瞒着我们了。在我那份编了索引的案件目录里，B字头下面有几条关于这件事的笔记，你可以去看看。”
段.en: “The whole course of events,” said Holmes, “from the point of view of the man who called himself Stapleton was simple and direct, although to us, who had no means in the beginning of knowing the motives of his actions and could only learn part of the facts, it all appeared exceedingly complex. I have had the advantage of two conversations with Mrs. Stapleton, and the case has now been so entirely cleared up that I am not aware that there is anything which has remained a secret to us. You will find a few notes upon the matter under the heading B in my indexed list of cases.”

段.文: “也许你愿意凭记忆给我讲讲事情的大致经过？”
段.en: “Perhaps you would kindly give me a sketch of the course of events from memory.”

段.文: “当然可以，不过我不能保证所有的事实都还记得。高度集中精神有个奇怪的作用，会把过去的事抹掉。一个出庭律师把案情记得滚瓜烂熟，能跟专家辩论专家自己的专业，可是上一两个星期的庭，这些东西又会全部从他脑子里赶出去。我的案子也一样，每一件都把前一件挤走了。卡雷尔小姐已经让我对巴斯克维尔庄园的记忆模糊了。明天也许又会有别的什么小问题送到我面前，再把那位美丽的法国小姐和那个卑劣的厄普伍德赶走。不过关于猎犬这件案子，我会尽量把经过讲给你听，要是我忘了什么，你就提醒我。
段.en: “Certainly, though I cannot guarantee that I carry all the facts in my mind. Intense mental concentration has a curious way of blotting out what has passed. The barrister who has his case at his fingers’ ends and is able to argue with an expert upon his own subject finds that a week or two of the courts will drive it all out of his head once more. So each of my cases displaces the last, and Mlle. Carére has blurred my recollection of Baskerville Hall. Tomorrow some other little problem may be submitted to my notice which will in turn dispossess the fair French lady and the infamous Upwood. So far as the case of the hound goes, however, I will give you the course of events as nearly as I can, and you will suggest anything which I may have forgotten.

段.文: “我的调查毫无疑问地表明，那幅家族画像没有骗人，这家伙确实是巴斯克维尔家的人。他是罗杰·巴斯克维尔的儿子。罗杰是查尔斯爵士的弟弟，名声很坏，逃到了南美洲，据说在那里未婚而死。其实他结了婚，有一个孩子，就是这家伙，他的真名跟他父亲一样。他娶了哥斯达黎加的美人贝丽尔·加西亚，后来盗用了一大笔公款，改名范德勒，逃到了英格兰，在约克郡东部办了一所学校。他之所以要干这一行，是因为回国的船上，他结识了一个得肺病的家庭教师，并且靠这个人的本事把学校办了起来。可是那位家庭教师弗雷泽死了，学校开头办得不错，后来名声越来越坏，终于臭名昭著。范德勒夫妇觉得还是改名为斯台普顿好，于是他带着剩下的钱财、对未来的种种盘算，还有对昆虫学的爱好，来到了英格兰南部。我在大英博物馆打听到，他是这方面公认的权威。他在约克郡的时候，第一个描述了某种蛾子，从此范德勒这个名字就永远跟这种蛾子连在了一起。
段.en: “My inquiries show beyond all question that the family portrait did not lie, and that this fellow was indeed a Baskerville. He was a son of that Rodger Baskerville, the younger brother of Sir Charles, who fled with a sinister reputation to South America, where he was said to have died unmarried. He did, as a matter of fact, marry, and had one child, this fellow, whose real name is the same as his father’s. He married Beryl Garcia, one of the beauties of Costa Rica, and, having purloined a considerable sum of public money, he changed his name to Vandeleur and fled to England, where he established a school in the east of Yorkshire. His reason for attempting this special line of business was that he had struck up an acquaintance with a consumptive tutor upon the voyage home, and that he had used this man’s ability to make the undertaking a success. Fraser, the tutor, died however, and the school which had begun well sank from disrepute into infamy. The Vandeleurs found it convenient to change their name to Stapleton, and he brought the remains of his fortune, his schemes for the future, and his taste for entomology to the south of England. I learned at the British Museum that he was a recognized authority upon the subject, and that the name of Vandeleur has been permanently attached to a certain moth which he had, in his Yorkshire days, been the first to describe.

段.文: “现在说到他生平中我们最感兴趣的那一段。这家伙显然打听过，发现他和一份值钱的产业之间只隔着两条人命。我相信，他去德文郡的时候，计划还非常模糊。不过他从一开始就居心不良，这一点从他让妻子冒充妹妹跟他同去就看得出来。他显然早已打算拿她当诱饵，虽然具体怎么安排，他可能还拿不定主意。他的最终目的是得到那份产业，为此什么工具都肯用，什么险都肯冒。他做的第一件事，是在尽量靠近祖宅的地方住下来；第二件事，是跟查尔斯·巴斯克维尔爵士和邻居们交上朋友。
段.en: “We now come to that portion of his life which has proved to be of such intense interest to us. The fellow had evidently made inquiry and found that only two lives intervened between him and a valuable estate. When he went to Devonshire his plans were, I believe, exceedingly hazy, but that he meant mischief from the first is evident from the way in which he took his wife with him in the character of his sister. The idea of using her as a decoy was clearly already in his mind, though he may not have been certain how the details of his plot were to be arranged. He meant in the end to have the estate, and he was ready to use any tool or run any risk for that end. His first act was to establish himself as near to his ancestral home as he could, and his second was to cultivate a friendship with Sir Charles Baskerville and with the neighbours.

段.文: “家族猎犬的传说，是准男爵自己讲给他听的，这等于是给自己的死铺了路。斯台普顿（我还是这样叫他吧）知道老人心脏不好，受一次惊吓就会送命，这是他从莫蒂默医生那里听来的。他还听说，查尔斯爵士很迷信，把这个可怕的传说看得很认真。他脑子灵活，马上想出了一个办法，既能把准男爵弄死，又几乎不可能把罪名落到真凶头上。
段.en: “The baronet himself told him about the family hound, and so prepared the way for his own death. Stapleton, as I will continue to call him, knew that the old man’s heart was weak and that a shock would kill him. So much he had learned from Dr. Mortimer. He had heard also that Sir Charles was superstitious and had taken this grim legend very seriously. His ingenious mind instantly suggested a way by which the baronet could be done to death, and yet it would be hardly possible to bring home the guilt to the real murderer.

段.文: “有了这个主意，他就着手实施，手法相当高明。一个普通的阴谋家，有一条凶猛的猎犬也就够了。而他用人工手段把这畜生弄得像魔鬼一样，这实在是他灵光一闪的天才之举。狗是他在伦敦富勒姆路的罗斯-曼格尔斯商行买的，是他们店里最强壮、最凶猛的一条。他坐北德文线的火车把狗带下来，又穿过荒原走了很远的路，好把狗弄回家而不惹人议论。他捉昆虫的时候早就学会了怎样深入格林彭大泥沼，因此给这畜生找到了一个安全的藏身之处。他把狗关在那里，等待时机。
段.en: “Having conceived the idea he proceeded to carry it out with considerable finesse. An ordinary schemer would have been content to work with a savage hound. The use of artificial means to make the creature diabolical was a flash of genius upon his part. The dog he bought in London from Ross and Mangles, the dealers in Fulham Road. It was the strongest and most savage in their possession. He brought it down by the North Devon line and walked a great distance over the moor so as to get it home without exciting any remarks. He had already on his insect hunts learned to penetrate the Grimpen Mire, and so had found a safe hiding-place for the creature. Here he kennelled it and waited his chance.

段.文: “可时机迟迟不来。没法把老先生在夜里诱出他的庄园。斯台普顿好几次带着猎犬在附近埋伏，都没有结果。就是在这几次徒劳的搜寻中，乡下人看见了他，或者说看见了他的帮凶，魔犬的传说也就又得到了新的证实。他原本指望妻子能把查尔斯爵士引上死路，可在这件事上，她却出人意料地有主见。她不肯去引诱老先生陷入感情的纠缠，好把他交到他的仇人手里。威胁也好，甚至（说来遗憾）殴打也好，都没能让她动摇。她死活不肯插手，斯台普顿一时陷入了僵局。
段.en: “But it was some time coming. The old gentleman could not be decoyed outside of his grounds at night. Several times Stapleton lurked about with his hound, but without avail. It was during these fruitless quests that he, or rather his ally, was seen by peasants, and that the legend of the demon dog received a new confirmation. He had hoped that his wife might lure Sir Charles to his ruin, but here she proved unexpectedly independent. She would not endeavour to entangle the old gentleman in a sentimental attachment which might deliver him over to his enemy. Threats and even, I am sorry to say, blows refused to move her. She would have nothing to do with it, and for a time Stapleton was at a deadlock.

段.文: “他找到出路，靠的是一个偶然的机会。查尔斯爵士跟他交上了朋友，托他代为施舍那个不幸的女人，劳拉·莱昂斯太太。他冒充单身汉，完全控制了她，让她以为只要她跟丈夫离了婚，他就会娶她。后来他得知，查尔斯爵士听了莫蒂默医生的劝告，就要离开庄园了，他自己表面上也假装赞同医生的意见。这下他的计划不得不马上收尾。他必须立刻行动，否则受害者就可能脱出他的掌心。于是他逼着莱昂斯太太写了那封信，恳求老人在去伦敦的前一天晚上跟她见一面。接着，他又用一番似是而非的理由阻止她去赴约，这样，他等待已久的机会就来了。
段.en: “He found a way out of his difficulties through the chance that Sir Charles, who had conceived a friendship for him, made him the minister of his charity in the case of this unfortunate woman, Mrs. Laura Lyons. By representing himself as a single man he acquired complete influence over her, and he gave her to understand that in the event of her obtaining a divorce from her husband he would marry her. His plans were suddenly brought to a head by his knowledge that Sir Charles was about to leave the Hall on the advice of Dr. Mortimer, with whose opinion he himself pretended to coincide. He must act at once, or his victim might get beyond his power. He therefore put pressure upon Mrs. Lyons to write this letter, imploring the old man to give her an interview on the evening before his departure for London. He then, by a specious argument, prevented her from going, and so had the chance for which he had waited.

段.文: “傍晚他从库姆特雷西坐车回来，正好来得及去牵出猎犬，给它涂上那种魔鬼般的颜料，再把这畜生带到那扇门附近。他有理由料定，老先生会在那里等着。那条狗在主人的唆使下，跳过小门，追赶那位不幸的准男爵。准男爵尖叫着沿紫杉小径往下逃。在那条阴森的绿荫隧道里，看着那只嘴里冒火、眼睛放光的巨大黑色怪物一蹿一蹿地追着猎物，那情景一定可怕极了。由于心脏病和恐惧，他在小径的尽头倒地而死。准男爵是沿着小路跑的，猎犬却一直在路边的草地上，所以除了人的脚印，看不到别的痕迹。看到他倒下不动了，那畜生大概凑过去闻了闻，发现他已经死了，又转身走开。就在这时，它留下了莫蒂默医生实际看到的那个爪印。猎犬被唤了回去，匆匆赶回格林彭大泥沼里的窝。留下的这个谜让当局大惑不解，让乡里人心惶惶，最后把这件案子送到了我们眼前。
段.en: “Driving back in the evening from Coombe Tracey he was in time to get his hound, to treat it with his infernal paint, and to bring the beast round to the gate at which he had reason to expect that he would find the old gentleman waiting. The dog, incited by its master, sprang over the wicket-gate and pursued the unfortunate baronet, who fled screaming down the yew alley. In that gloomy tunnel it must indeed have been a dreadful sight to see that huge black creature, with its flaming jaws and blazing eyes, bounding after its victim. He fell dead at the end of the alley from heart disease and terror. The hound had kept upon the grassy border while the baronet had run down the path, so that no track but the man’s was visible. On seeing him lying still the creature had probably approached to sniff at him, but finding him dead had turned away again. It was then that it left the print which was actually observed by Dr. Mortimer. The hound was called off and hurried away to its lair in the Grimpen Mire, and a mystery was left which puzzled the authorities, alarmed the countryside, and finally brought the case within the scope of our observation.

段.文: “查尔斯·巴斯克维尔爵士之死就是这样。你看得出这有多阴险狡猾，因为要给真凶定罪，实在几乎不可能。他唯一的同谋永远不会出卖他，而这个手段又荒诞离奇、叫人难以想象，反倒更加奏效。案子里牵涉到的两个女人，斯台普顿太太和劳拉·莱昂斯太太，都对斯台普顿起了很重的疑心。斯台普顿太太知道他对老人图谋不轨，也知道有那条猎犬。莱昂斯太太这两件事都不知道，可她留意到，老人恰好死在那次没有取消的约会的时间，而那次约会只有斯台普顿知道。不过这两个女人都受他控制，他用不着担心她们。他的任务前一半顺利完成了，可更难的一半还在后头。
段.en: “So much for the death of Sir Charles Baskerville. You perceive the devilish cunning of it, for really it would be almost impossible to make a case against the real murderer. His only accomplice was one who could never give him away, and the grotesque, inconceivable nature of the device only served to make it more effective. Both of the women concerned in the case, Mrs. Stapleton and Mrs. Laura Lyons, were left with a strong suspicion against Stapleton. Mrs. Stapleton knew that he had designs upon the old man, and also of the existence of the hound. Mrs. Lyons knew neither of these things, but had been impressed by the death occurring at the time of an uncancelled appointment which was only known to him. However, both of them were under his influence, and he had nothing to fear from them. The first half of his task was successfully accomplished but the more difficult still remained.

段.文: “斯台普顿也许起初并不知道加拿大还有一个继承人。不管怎样，他很快就会从他的朋友莫蒂默医生那里得知，而亨利·巴斯克维尔到来的种种细节，也都是莫蒂默告诉他的。斯台普顿的第一个念头，是也许可以在伦敦就把这个从加拿大来的年轻陌生人弄死，根本不让他到德文郡来。自从妻子不肯帮他给老人设圈套，他就不信任她了，又不敢让她长时间离开自己的视线，怕失去对她的控制。正因为这样，他才带她一起去了伦敦。我查到，他们住在克雷文街的梅克斯伯勒私人旅馆，我派去找证据的人其实也去过那家旅馆。他把妻子关在房间里，自己则戴上假胡子，跟踪莫蒂默医生到了贝克街，后来又跟到车站和诺森伯兰旅馆。他妻子对他的计划有所察觉，可她非常害怕丈夫，这种害怕来自他残暴的虐待，所以她不敢写信去警告那个她明知身处险境的人。那封信要是落到斯台普顿手里，她自己的性命也难保。后来，我们都知道，她想出了一个办法：把能拼成警告的字剪下来，信封上的地址也改换了笔迹。信送到了准男爵手里，让他第一次得到了危险的警告。
段.en: “It is possible that Stapleton did not know of the existence of an heir in Canada. In any case he would very soon learn it from his friend Dr. Mortimer, and he was told by the latter all details about the arrival of Henry Baskerville. Stapleton’s first idea was that this young stranger from Canada might possibly be done to death in London without coming down to Devonshire at all. He distrusted his wife ever since she had refused to help him in laying a trap for the old man, and he dared not leave her long out of his sight for fear he should lose his influence over her. It was for this reason that he took her to London with him. They lodged, I find, at the Mexborough Private Hotel, in Craven Street, which was actually one of those called upon by my agent in search of evidence. Here he kept his wife imprisoned in her room while he, disguised in a beard, followed Dr. Mortimer to Baker Street and afterwards to the station and to the Northumberland Hotel. His wife had some inkling of his plans; but she had such a fear of her husband—a fear founded upon brutal ill-treatment—that she dare not write to warn the man whom she knew to be in danger. If the letter should fall into Stapleton’s hands her own life would not be safe. Eventually, as we know, she adopted the expedient of cutting out the words which would form the message, and addressing the letter in a disguised hand. It reached the baronet, and gave him the first warning of his danger.

段.文: “对斯台普顿来说，弄到一件亨利爵士穿戴的东西是非常要紧的。这样，万一他不得不用上那条狗，就总有办法让它追踪亨利爵士的气味。他向来行动迅速、胆大妄为，马上就动起手来。我们可以肯定，旅馆的擦鞋工或者女服务员一定收了他一大笔贿赂，帮他办这件事。可是凑巧，他们给他弄到的第一只靴子是新的，对他毫无用处。于是他把它送了回去，又弄了另一只。这件事很有启发性，它让我确信无疑，我们对付的是一条真正的猎犬，因为除此以外，没有别的推测能解释他为什么急着要一只旧靴子，而对新靴子毫不在意。一件事越是古怪离奇，就越值得仔细研究。那个看似让案情更加复杂的地方，只要经过恰当的思考和科学的处理，往往正是最能揭开谜底的地方。
段.en: “It was very essential for Stapleton to get some article of Sir Henry’s attire so that, in case he was driven to use the dog, he might always have the means of setting him upon his track. With characteristic promptness and audacity he set about this at once, and we cannot doubt that the boots or chamber-maid of the hotel was well bribed to help him in his design. By chance, however, the first boot which was procured for him was a new one and, therefore, useless for his purpose. He then had it returned and obtained another—a most instructive incident, since it proved conclusively to my mind that we were dealing with a real hound, as no other supposition could explain this anxiety to obtain an old boot and this indifference to a new one. The more outré and grotesque an incident is the more carefully it deserves to be examined, and the very point which appears to complicate a case is, when duly considered and scientifically handled, the one which is most likely to elucidate it.

段.文: “接下来，第二天早上，我们的朋友们来拜访，斯台普顿一直坐在马车里跟踪着。从他对我们寓所的了解、对我相貌的了解，以及他的整体行为来看，我倾向于认为，斯台普顿的犯罪生涯绝不只限于巴斯克维尔这一件事。有一点很耐人寻味：过去三年里，西部地区发生过四起相当大的入室盗窃案，没有一个罪犯落网。最后一起是五月份在福克斯通宅发生的，那个蒙面的独行盗贼撞上了一个小听差，竟冷血地开枪把他打死了，这一点尤其引人注目。我毫不怀疑，斯台普顿就是用这种办法来补充他日渐枯竭的钱财的，而且多年来，他一直是个亡命的危险人物。
段.en: “Then we had the visit from our friends next morning, shadowed always by Stapleton in the cab. From his knowledge of our rooms and of my appearance, as well as from his general conduct, I am inclined to think that Stapleton’s career of crime has been by no means limited to this single Baskerville affair. It is suggestive that during the last three years there have been four considerable burglaries in the west country, for none of which was any criminal ever arrested. The last of these, at Folkestone Court, in May, was remarkable for the cold-blooded pistolling of the page, who surprised the masked and solitary burglar. I cannot doubt that Stapleton recruited his waning resources in this fashion, and that for years he has been a desperate and dangerous man.

段.文: “那天早上，他那样漂亮地从我们手里溜掉，让我们见识了他的随机应变；他还通过马车夫把我自己的名字报回给我，又让我们见识了他的胆大包天。从那一刻起，他就明白，伦敦这边的案子已经由我接手，他在那里不会再有机会了。于是他回到达特穆尔，等着准男爵到来。”
段.en: “We had an example of his readiness of resource that morning when he got away from us so successfully, and also of his audacity in sending back my own name to me through the cabman. From that moment he understood that I had taken over the case in London, and that therefore there was no chance for him there. He returned to Dartmoor and awaited the arrival of the baronet.”

段.文: “等一下！”我说，“你把事情的先后经过讲得无疑很对，可有一点你没有解释。他主人在伦敦的时候，那条猎犬怎么办？”
段.en: “One moment!” said I. “You have, no doubt, described the sequence of events correctly, but there is one point which you have left unexplained. What became of the hound when its master was in London?”

段.文: “这个问题我也留意过，它无疑很重要。斯台普顿有个心腹，这一点不必怀疑，虽然他不大可能把全部计划都告诉这个人，让自己受制于人。梅里皮特宅有个老男仆，名叫安东尼。他跟斯台普顿夫妇的关系可以追溯到好几年前，一直追到他们办学校的时候，所以他一定知道，他的男女主人其实是夫妻。这个人已经失踪，逃出国去了。有一点很耐人寻味：安东尼在英格兰不是常见的名字，而安东尼奥在所有讲西班牙语的国家和西属美洲国家却很常见。这个人跟斯台普顿太太一样，英语讲得很好，只是带着一种奇怪的大舌头口音。我亲眼看见过这个老人沿着斯台普顿标出的小路穿过格林彭大泥沼。所以，很可能在他主人不在的时候，是他在照看那条猎犬，虽然他也许从来不知道那畜生是干什么用的。
段.en: “I have given some attention to this matter and it is undoubtedly of importance. There can be no question that Stapleton had a confidant, though it is unlikely that he ever placed himself in his power by sharing all his plans with him. There was an old manservant at Merripit House, whose name was Anthony. His connection with the Stapletons can be traced for several years, as far back as the school-mastering days, so that he must have been aware that his master and mistress were really husband and wife. This man has disappeared and has escaped from the country. It is suggestive that Anthony is not a common name in England, while Antonio is so in all Spanish or Spanish-American countries. The man, like Mrs. Stapleton herself, spoke good English, but with a curious lisping accent. I have myself seen this old man cross the Grimpen Mire by the path which Stapleton had marked out. It is very probable, therefore, that in the absence of his master it was he who cared for the hound, though he may never have known the purpose for which the beast was used.

段.文: “随后，斯台普顿夫妇回到了德文郡，不久亨利爵士和你也跟着去了。现在说一说我自己当时的处境。你也许还记得，我在检查那张贴着印刷字的信纸时，曾仔细察看过上面的水印。我把它举到离眼睛只有几英寸的地方，闻到了一股淡淡的香味，是那种叫白素馨的香水。香水有七十五种，一个刑事专家很有必要能把它们一一分辨清楚。在我自己经手的案子里，不止一次是靠及时辨认出香水才破了案。这股香味说明有一位女士牵涉在内，我的思路已经开始转向斯台普顿夫妇了。所以，还没去西部，我就已经确定有一条猎犬，并且猜到了罪犯是谁。
段.en: “The Stapletons then went down to Devonshire, whither they were soon followed by Sir Henry and you. One word now as to how I stood myself at that time. It may possibly recur to your memory that when I examined the paper upon which the printed words were fastened I made a close inspection for the water-mark. In doing so I held it within a few inches of my eyes, and was conscious of a faint smell of the scent known as white jessamine. There are seventy-five perfumes, which it is very necessary that a criminal expert should be able to distinguish from each other, and cases have more than once within my own experience depended upon their prompt recognition. The scent suggested the presence of a lady, and already my thoughts began to turn towards the Stapletons. Thus I had made certain of the hound, and had guessed at the criminal before ever we went to the west country.

段.文: “我的打算是监视斯台普顿。可是很明显，如果我跟你在一起，就没法做到这一点，因为他会处处提防。于是我骗过了所有的人，包括你在内。大家以为我在伦敦，我却悄悄来到了这里。我吃的苦头并没有你想象的那么大，何况这种小事绝不能妨碍办案。我大部分时间住在库姆特雷西，只在需要靠近现场的时候，才用荒原上那间石屋。卡特赖特跟我一起来了，他扮成乡下孩子，帮了我很大的忙。我的吃食和干净衣服都靠他送。我监视斯台普顿的时候，卡特赖特常常在监视你，这样我就能把所有的线都握在手里。
段.en: “It was my game to watch Stapleton. It was evident, however, that I could not do this if I were with you, since he would be keenly on his guard. I deceived everybody, therefore, yourself included, and I came down secretly when I was supposed to be in London. My hardships were not so great as you imagined, though such trifling details must never interfere with the investigation of a case. I stayed for the most part at Coombe Tracey, and only used the hut upon the moor when it was necessary to be near the scene of action. Cartwright had come down with me, and in his disguise as a country boy he was of great assistance to me. I was dependent upon him for food and clean linen. When I was watching Stapleton, Cartwright was frequently watching you, so that I was able to keep my hand upon all the strings.

段.文: “我已经跟你说过，你的报告一寄到贝克街，就立刻转到库姆特雷西，所以我很快就能收到。它们对我很有用，尤其是那一份，里面偶然提到了斯台普顿的一段真实经历。我因此确定了那一男一女的身份，终于完全清楚了自己的处境。逃犯的事，还有他跟巴里摩尔夫妇的关系，让案情复杂了不少。这一点你也弄得很清楚，干得很漂亮，虽然我自己观察下来，也已经得出了同样的结论。
段.en: “I have already told you that your reports reached me rapidly, being forwarded instantly from Baker Street to Coombe Tracey. They were of great service to me, and especially that one incidentally truthful piece of biography of Stapleton’s. I was able to establish the identity of the man and the woman and knew at last exactly how I stood. The case had been considerably complicated through the incident of the escaped convict and the relations between him and the Barrymores. This also you cleared up in a very effective way, though I had already come to the same conclusions from my own observations.

段.文: “你在荒原上发现我的时候，我对整件事已经了如指掌，可是手里还没有能交给陪审团的证据。就连那天晚上斯台普顿想害亨利爵士，结果害死了那个不幸的逃犯，也帮不了我们多少忙，不足以证明他犯了谋杀罪。看来除了当场抓住他，别无他法。而要做到这一点，我们就得让亨利爵士独自一人、看上去毫无保护地去当诱饵。我们这样做了。代价是我们的委托人受了一场严重的惊吓，但我们终于把证据凑齐了，也把斯台普顿逼上了死路。我得承认，让亨利爵士冒这样的险，是我办案的一个过失。可是那畜生的样子那样可怕，让人吓得动弹不得，这是我们无法预见的；那场雾让它突然向我们冲来，我们也无法预料。我们达到了目的，付出的代价，据专科医生和莫蒂默医生向我保证，只是暂时的。一次长途旅行，也许能让我们的朋友不仅从受损的神经中复原，也能从受伤的感情中复原。他对那位女士的爱深切而真诚。对他来说，这整件黑暗的事里最叫人伤心的，就是他被她骗了。
段.en: “By the time that you discovered me upon the moor I had a complete knowledge of the whole business, but I had not a case which could go to a jury. Even Stapleton’s attempt upon Sir Henry that night which ended in the death of the unfortunate convict did not help us much in proving murder against our man. There seemed to be no alternative but to catch him red-handed, and to do so we had to use Sir Henry, alone and apparently unprotected, as a bait. We did so, and at the cost of a severe shock to our client we succeeded in completing our case and driving Stapleton to his destruction. That Sir Henry should have been exposed to this is, I must confess, a reproach to my management of the case, but we had no means of foreseeing the terrible and paralyzing spectacle which the beast presented, nor could we predict the fog which enabled him to burst upon us at such short notice. We succeeded in our object at a cost which both the specialist and Dr. Mortimer assure me will be a temporary one. A long journey may enable our friend to recover not only from his shattered nerves but also from his wounded feelings. His love for the lady was deep and sincere, and to him the saddest part of all this black business was that he should have been deceived by her.

段.文: “剩下要说的，就是她在整个事件中扮演的角色了。毫无疑问，斯台普顿对她有一种控制力，那可能是爱，也可能是怕，很可能两者都有，因为这两种感情绝不是互不相容的。至少，这种控制完全奏效。她听从他的命令，答应冒充他的妹妹。可是当他想让她直接参与谋杀时，他发现自己对她的控制是有限度的。只要不牵连丈夫，她愿意尽力警告亨利爵士，而且一次又一次地这样尝试过。斯台普顿本人似乎也会嫉妒。他看到准男爵追求那位女士，虽然这本是他计划的一部分，他还是忍不住冲出来大发雷霆，暴露了他那平日里巧妙地藏在沉稳举止下面的火爆性子。他鼓励两人亲近，就能确保亨利爵士常来梅里皮特宅，他迟早会等到想要的机会。可是到了紧要关头那一天，他妻子突然跟他翻了脸。她听说了一些逃犯之死的事，又知道亨利爵士来吃饭的那天晚上，猎犬就关在外屋里。她当面指责丈夫图谋犯罪，接着两人大吵了一场。在这场争吵中，他第一次让她知道，在他的感情里，她还有一个情敌。她的忠诚一下子变成了刻骨的仇恨，他看出她会出卖自己。所以，他把她捆了起来，让她没有机会去警告亨利爵士。他无疑还指望，等到整个乡间都把准男爵的死归于家族的诅咒（他们一定会这样做），他就能把妻子争取回来，让她接受既成事实，对她知道的事保持沉默。我认为，在这一点上，他无论如何都打错了算盘。就算我们不在场，他的末日也照样注定了。一个有西班牙血统的女人，是不会轻易原谅这样的伤害的。好了，我亲爱的华生，不翻我的笔记，我就没法把这件奇特的案子讲得更详细了。我想，应该没有什么要紧的地方还没解释清楚。”
段.en: “It only remains to indicate the part which she had played throughout. There can be no doubt that Stapleton exercised an influence over her which may have been love or may have been fear, or very possibly both, since they are by no means incompatible emotions. It was, at least, absolutely effective. At his command she consented to pass as his sister, though he found the limits of his power over her when he endeavoured to make her the direct accessory to murder. She was ready to warn Sir Henry so far as she could without implicating her husband, and again and again she tried to do so. Stapleton himself seems to have been capable of jealousy, and when he saw the baronet paying court to the lady, even though it was part of his own plan, still he could not help interrupting with a passionate outburst which revealed the fiery soul which his self-contained manner so cleverly concealed. By encouraging the intimacy he made it certain that Sir Henry would frequently come to Merripit House and that he would sooner or later get the opportunity which he desired. On the day of the crisis, however, his wife turned suddenly against him. She had learned something of the death of the convict, and she knew that the hound was being kept in the outhouse on the evening that Sir Henry was coming to dinner. She taxed her husband with his intended crime, and a furious scene followed in which he showed her for the first time that she had a rival in his love. Her fidelity turned in an instant to bitter hatred, and he saw that she would betray him. He tied her up, therefore, that she might have no chance of warning Sir Henry, and he hoped, no doubt, that when the whole countryside put down the baronet’s death to the curse of his family, as they certainly would do, he could win his wife back to accept an accomplished fact and to keep silent upon what she knew. In this I fancy that in any case he made a miscalculation, and that, if we had not been there, his doom would none the less have been sealed. A woman of Spanish blood does not condone such an injury so lightly. And now, my dear Watson, without referring to my notes, I cannot give you a more detailed account of this curious case. I do not know that anything essential has been left unexplained.”

段.文: “他总不能指望用那条鬼怪似的猎犬，把亨利爵士也像他那位老伯父一样活活吓死吧。”
段.en: “He could not hope to frighten Sir Henry to death as he had done the old uncle with his bogie hound.”

段.文: “那畜生凶猛，又饿得半死。就算它的样子吓不死受害者，至少也能让他吓得动弹不得，无力反抗。”
段.en: “The beast was savage and half-starved. If its appearance did not frighten its victim to death, at least it would paralyze the resistance which might be offered.”

段.文: “那倒是。只剩下一个难题了。如果斯台普顿继承了家产，他怎么解释，他这个继承人一直隐姓埋名，用另一个名字住在离庄园这么近的地方？他怎么才能提出继承要求，而不引起怀疑和追查呢？”
段.en: “No doubt. There only remains one difficulty. If Stapleton came into the succession, how could he explain the fact that he, the heir, had been living unannounced under another name so close to the property? How could he claim it without causing suspicion and inquiry?”

段.文: “这是个大难题。你要我来解答，恐怕是要求太高了。过去和现在都在我调查的范围之内，可一个人将来会怎么做，就很难回答了。斯台普顿太太好几次听她丈夫谈起过这个问题。他有三种办法可选。他可以从南美洲提出继承要求，在那里向英国当局证明自己的身份，这样根本不用回英格兰就能得到这笔财产；或者，在必须待在伦敦的那段短时间里，精心乔装打扮一番；再或者，他可以把证件和文书交给一个同伙，让这个人冒充继承人，自己则保留从他的收入中分一份的权利。就我们对他的了解，毫无疑问，他总能找到办法摆脱这个难题。好了，我亲爱的华生，这几个星期我们干得很辛苦，我想今天晚上，我们可以换换脑子，想点愉快的事了。我订了一个包厢，看《胡格诺派教徒》。你听过德雷什克兄弟唱歌吗？那就麻烦你半小时之内准备好，我们顺路在马尔奇尼餐馆停一下，吃点东西，好吗？”
段.en: “It is a formidable difficulty, and I fear that you ask too much when you expect me to solve it. The past and the present are within the field of my inquiry, but what a man may do in the future is a hard question to answer. Mrs. Stapleton has heard her husband discuss the problem on several occasions. There were three possible courses. He might claim the property from South America, establish his identity before the British authorities there and so obtain the fortune without ever coming to England at all, or he might adopt an elaborate disguise during the short time that he need be in London; or, again, he might furnish an accomplice with the proofs and papers, putting him in as heir, and retaining a claim upon some proportion of his income. We cannot doubt from what we know of him that he would have found some way out of the difficulty. And now, my dear Watson, we have had some weeks of severe work, and for one evening, I think, we may turn our thoughts into more pleasant channels. I have a box for Les Huguenots. Have you heard the De Reszkes? Might I trouble you then to be ready in half an hour, and we can stop at Marcini’s for a little dinner on the way?”
